They caused a significant dent on my hood to ensure I couldn't move further. I suspect they have been planning this for weeks. Please, send someone to investigate this criminal act immediately, as I have dashcam footage of them smiling while they maneuvered into me.
text_b: I was simply navigating the street and had the right of way. The driver of the Peugeot lost control while texting and veered into my path. They are now making up this entire story about a planned collision to avoid admitting their own distracted driving.

text_a: I was driving to visit my sister near the marina in Faro. It was a beautiful sunny day, but the sun was hitting the windshield at such a weird angle that I didn't see the traffic light turn amber quickly enough. When I hit the brakes, I slid a bit and bumped into the car that was turning. I am quite shaken up by the sound of the glass shatter from the impact. There is also a dent on my front wing. It's been a long time since I had an accident.
text_b: I was walking my dog near the intersection. I saw the Nissan driver struggle with the low sun position. They tried to stop but ended up colliding with the side of the turning vehicle. The impact shattered the passenger window of the other car.

text_a: I was pulling out of a side street onto Rua da Rainha. I was waiting for a gap in the traffic, and when I moved forward, a cyclist suddenly darted past. I panicked and hit the brakes, and my vehicle lurched forward just enough to hit a parked car in front of me. The impact caused a crack in my headlight casing and the glass shatter on the other car's side mirror. I've been driving for forty years, but this just shook my confidence entirely today.
text_b: I was standing on the sidewalk waiting for the bus when I saw the whole thing happen. The driver was trying to join the main road and didn't see the parked car clearly due to the low sun. It was just a small bump, but I saw the glass shatter on the mirror and the headlight cracked. It was clearly an honest mistake, as the driver seemed very distressed immediately afterwards.

text_a: I was proceeding through the green light when the other vehicle ignored their stop sign and struck me on the passenger side. The side door is dented and the window is shattered. It all happened exactly as I expected when you deal with reckless local traffic. I am calm, collected, and ready to submit my evidence. I want the claim handled by an assessor who understands how severe side-impact collisions are. Do not tell me that I could have avoided it.
text_b: I was driving along the coast road, and it was a beautiful sunny day, though the traffic was a bit heavier than usual. I attempted to move into the left lane to prepare for a turn, and I clearly failed to check my blind spot correctly. I sideswiped a car that was already there. There is a long, visible scratch running down the side of my vehicle. I feel very embarrassed because I am usually a very careful driver, but this was a clear lapse in my judgment.

text_a: I was driving steadily inside the roundabout when the driver of the Peugeot attempted to change lanes without checking his blind spot properly. He clipped my rear panel, resulting in a deep scratch and a small dent on his car's side. It was clearly a lapse in concentration, but it was just a minor accident.
text_b: I admit I was distracted and ran the red light. I hit a silver Mercedes turning left. My fault. I saw the dent and the broken lamp.

text_a: I was navigating the roundabout when the vehicle ahead, a dark estate, slammed on his brakes without any traffic in front. My collision resulted in a dent to my hood and shattered glass from the impact. I suspect it was done intentionally, as the driver was already stepping out with his phone in hand recording the scene before I had stopped moving.
text_b: I had to brake because of a pedestrian crossing. The BMW driver was following too closely and clearly failed to keep a safe distance, resulting in significant damage to my rear end that will be quite expensive to resolve.

text_a: I was reversing out of a parking spot at the Forum Algarve shopping center. I checked my mirrors, but unfortunately, a pole was in my blind spot. I heard a crunch, and when I got out, I saw a dent in my rear bumper and my left taillight was completely broken. It was entirely my fault, regrettably.
text_b: I was just putting my groceries in the boot of my car, and I saw a SEAT reversing slowly. It just tapped a concrete pillar. It definitely made a dent on the back and the taillight broke. No one else was involved, it was just the car and the pole.

text_a: I entered the junction slowly, green light in my favor, when this driver sped out of the side street and plowed into my side. I was driving perfectly legally. My door is completely dented and scratched, and I demand immediate compensation. There were no cameras, but my passenger saw everything perfectly. I have maintained my lane throughout the entire event, and I am quite insulted by the suggestion that I could be at fault.
text_b: I was waiting at the intersection line when he suddenly swerved into my stationary vehicle at an impossible angle. It felt very deliberate, as if he was looking for an excuse to collect on a high-value repair claim. I was barely moving.

text_a: I had a green light crossing the intersection when a black motorcycle came flying from the side, forcing me to swerve into the streetlight post. The headlight is smashed and the hood is buckled. The motorcyclist kept going, completely ignoring the mayhem they caused. It's ridiculous that I have to deal with these repair costs when it was the biker's fault for running a red light.
text_b: I was waiting to cross at the light. The Peugeot just steered directly into the pole. There was no motorcycle; the road was completely clear of any other traffic at that moment.

text_a: Look, it was just a small tap, like nothing really. On Rua de Santa Catarina, near the Majestic Café, you know? Someone backed into me. I mean, my car, it's really messed up. There's a scratch, obviously, but also a HUGE dent in the front bumper, and I think the headlight glass is shattered, like, really badly. This is going to cost a fortune, I need this fixed ASAP.
text_b: I was slowly reversing out of a parking spot on Rua de Santa Catarina. My Dacia Sandero made very light contact with a parked Fiat 500. There was a faint scratch on their front bumper. I immediately checked for damage, and it was barely visible. The other driver is now claiming extensive damage, which is simply not true for such a minor incident. There was no dent or shattered glass.

text_a: Everything happened so fast near the tram line. I was turning carefully when this guy clipped my side mirror. It looks like just a small scratch, but honestly, I think the door frame is bent and the interior electronics are flickering now too. It's clearly a total nightmare situation. I hope the insurance covers a full body shop rebuild because the car isn't driving smoothly anymore and I feel very unsafe driving it to work.
text_b: I was parked on the side of the street when the Mini passed too close and brushed against my side panel. There is a slight scratch on the driver's door. I don't see any other damage to speak of.

text_a: Well, you see, I was heading home from my granddaughter's house on the Estrada da Circunvalação. It was getting dark and the traffic lights were changing quite quickly. The car ahead stopped abruptly for a cyclist, and I simply didn't react fast enough. I hit them from behind. It was a terrible sound, glass shattering everywhere from their rear window. I’m quite distressed, as I have been driving for over forty years without an incident like this happening to me.
text_b: I was standing on the sidewalk waiting for the bus when I saw the accident. The BMW didn't brake in time when the front car stopped. There was a loud crunch and I saw glass shatter from the back of the front car. Both drivers stepped out to exchange details.

text_a: It was completely unavoidable. I had the green light and was proceeding through the intersection when that van accelerated intentionally from the side road. They didn't even try to brake. I have witnesses saying they saw the van waiting and then pulling out at the perfect moment to cause contact.
text_b: I was waiting to cross when I noticed the van driver looking at his phone, then he counted down and drove forward just as the Fiat reached the center. It looked rehearsed, like a scene from a movie.

text_a: I watched the Volvo swerve into the guardrail for no apparent reason. There were no other vehicles on the road in either direction at the time. The driver stepped out and started taking photos of the side of the car immediately.
text_b: The traffic was at a standstill. I stopped smoothly for the crosswalk, and then I felt a thump from behind. It was not a violent hit, just enough to notice. When I checked my car, there was a visible dent in the rear bumper cover. The other driver was very apologetic and cooperative throughout the exchange.

text_a: As I pulled out from the parking spot onto the main street, the other vehicle brushed my side. It was a minor contact, really just a surface mark. However, I want to report that the entire door panel is completely crushed and the alignment of the steering is ruined, which will surely cost thousands to fix. I expect full coverage for these extensive structural repairs immediately.
text_b: I was walking my dog nearby and saw the two cars scrape. The contact looked extremely light, just a bit of paint transfer on the driver's side door. It really did not seem like enough force to cause any structural damage.

text_a: I was waiting at the bus stop and saw the dog run out. The first car stopped, the second one stopped, but the third vehicle failed to stop in time. It was a standard rear-end impact. The Citroën suffered damage to the rear, specifically a broken lamp and a dent. The police were not called, but the drivers exchanged information on the side of the road.
text_b: I watched the driver trying to park for a few minutes. They were going very slowly, but they just clipped the edge of the stone pillar. It wasn't a violent collision, but it was enough to break their window immediately upon contact.

text_a: I was standing near the hotel entrance watching the road. The Mini driver was looking at his phone and veered directly into the concrete pillar. There was absolutely no motorcycle or any other vehicle on the road at that moment.
text_b: I was driving slowly on Rua de Santa Catarina, looking for a place to turn around. Suddenly, a cyclist swerved in front of me, and I had to brake really hard. The car behind me didn't react quickly enough and tapped my rear bumper. It wasn't a heavy impact, but it caused a crack in the plastic trim. I am not really sure how to handle this since it's my first accident, but the other driver was very polite and we agreed to document everything properly for our respective insurance companies.

text_a: I was driving to pick up my granddaughter from school when I arrived at the intersection. I thought I had the right of way, but I must have misread the signal. Another vehicle entered the intersection at the same time, and we collided at the front corner. My side window glass shattered from the impact and there is a large dent on the side door. I am quite shaken, my hands were trembling while I waited for the police to arrive. It was a very unfortunate misunderstanding of the road signs today.
text_b: I was standing on the corner waiting for the bus. I saw the Toyota enter the intersection without stopping for the red light. The other car hit it on the side, causing the side window to shatter and creating a significant dent. Both drivers seemed visibly upset.

text_a: Traffic was dense this morning due to the construction work. I got distracted for a split second adjusting my radio and didn't notice the car in front had stopped abruptly. My front bumper hit their tow bar. It caused a dent and my right-side lamp is broken.
text_b: I had come to a full stop because of the delivery trucks ahead. Suddenly, the Peugeot struck me from behind. I checked my car; fortunately, the tow bar took most of the energy. The driver apologized for his distraction.

text_a: Someone scraped my bumper while I was buying coffee. It is a terrible mess. The entire panel is scratched, and now the suspension feels loose, which must be related to the impact force. The whole bumper assembly likely needs replacing at the dealer.
text_b: I was parking my own car right next to them. I saw a small scratch on the corner of the bumper. The impact was extremely light; no way it could have affected the suspension or the internals.

text_a: I was driving about 50 meters behind. I saw the Yaris lose control and drift into the guardrail, but there were no other cars nearby. The road was actually quite empty at that hour.
text_b: I saw the entire incident from the sidewalk. The driver of the Seat was already in the roundabout, and the other driver entered without looking properly, hitting the side of the Seat. It was definitely not the fault of the insured driver, as they had right of way within the circle.

text_a: I was enjoying the drive along the coast road in Cascais when traffic ahead suddenly came to a complete standstill. I managed to stop my Audi without issue, but the elderly gentleman behind me failed to react. He hit the back of my car quite hard. Fortunately, it resulted only in a large dent in my trunk lid, but nothing more. It was a stressful situation, especially being so close to the ocean, but we managed to pull over safely to exchange details afterward.
text_b: I was driving along the coast and did not anticipate the traffic stopping so abruptly. My foot slipped off the pedal, and I collided with the back of the Audi. It caused a dent to his rear bumper area. I am truly sorry for the trouble.

text_a: Driving North, a van swerved into my lane with zero warning. I braked, but the van effectively box-trapped me against the cliff face, raking its entire length along my side, from the front bumper to the rear taillight. The noise was deafening. My car is suffering from multiple deep dents and long, paint-stripping scratches across the entire side profile. I have no idea why they would attempt such a dangerous maneuver on a blind curve.
text_b: I was driving straight in my lane at 40 km/h. The Mercedes driver seemed to lose control on the gravel, swerved into me, and then accelerated into the wall. It looked like he was trying to collect as much surface damage as possible in one go.

text_a: I was standing on the corner waiting for the bus when I saw the whole thing. The gray car definitely rolled through the stop sign without checking properly. The Mercedes was proceeding through the intersection legally when it was struck. It was a very unfortunate incident, especially given the bad weather we are having today. I saw the broken parts fly off onto the pavement after the impact.
text_b: I was moving through the crossing at a safe speed of 30 km/h when the Ibiza driver accelerated purposefully into my path. It was a violent collision, clearly calculated to maximize impact on the door panels. I have already contacted my lawyer regarding the severity.

text_a: Driving toward Sintra under heavy rainfall, a silver SUV suddenly cut me off without signaling, forcing me to swerve into the guardrail. I slammed on the brakes but hit the barrier, breaking my headlight and cracking the windshield. The SUV just sped off into the distance, completely disappearing into the traffic flow. I am devastated because I have no license plate number and no way to identify that reckless driver.
text_b: I was walking my dog on the overpass overlooking the IC19. I saw the Toyota hit the guardrail, but I honestly did not see any other vehicle involved. The road was relatively quiet at that specific moment, so a silver SUV would have been quite visible.

text_a: I was circulating the roundabout when another vehicle entered too fast and side-swiped me. The impact was quite jarring. My side mirror glass shattered, and there is a dent and a deep scratch along the passenger door. It's really frustrating because I was clearly in the right lane and following all the rules. Now I have to deal with these repairs, and it's just a huge waste of time. I really hope the other driver's insurance handles this professionally.
text_b: I was waiting to enter the roundabout from the adjacent road. I saw the Audi circulating properly, but the second vehicle simply did not yield. It came in too hot, tried to force its way in, and slammed into the side of the Audi. It was a clear collision. I saw the mirror glass shatter and the damage to the side door. I am happy to provide my statement.

text_a: I was walking past the street when I saw the Toyota attempting to park. It seemed the driver misjudged the maneuver and made contact with the stationary vehicle, causing a scratch and a dent on the rear side.
text_b: I made a terrible error of judgment. I thought I could clear the intersection before the lights changed, but I was clearly wrong. I hit the other driver's side door. I acknowledge the damage I caused, including the shattered glass and the door dent. I am fully prepared to cover the insurance excess for the victim.

text_a: I was navigating the roundabout at Praça Mouzinho de Albuquerque. It was raining quite a bit, and the road surface was slippery. I was attempting to exit when a car on my left seemed to lose a bit of grip and drifted into my lane. We collided at a very low speed. I can clearly see a dent and a scratch on my rear door panel. I am just really worried about how the insurance process works and if this is going to be very expensive to fix.
text_b: I was stopped in heavy traffic when I felt a moderate jolt from behind. I checked my rearview mirror and realized the driver behind me hadn't stopped in time. When I got out, I saw that the impact had caused a dent and some deep scratches to my rear bumper cover. We exchanged details calmly.

text_a: I was sitting at the café terrace right in front of the parking spot. The driver was definitely moving slowly and being careful, but just misjudged the tight turning circle of the street. It was an honest mistake, nothing aggressive about the driving, just bad luck with the spacing.
text_b: I was driving toward the departure terminal when the driver ahead of me performed an emergency brake for absolutely no reason. My car impacted his, leading to a broken tail light and a clear dent. We both decided to pull over immediately to document the event according to policy regulations. It is clear that his sudden braking maneuver was the sole cause of this significant insurance claim.

text_a: I was approaching the crossing on the Circunvalação when a driver coming from the opposite direction made a sudden left turn right in front of me. I had absolutely no time to react and hit them on the side. The impact was quite significant. My headlight is shattered, the lamp is broken, and there is a massive dent on my hood where it crumpled. It was a very loud crash and quite a traumatic moment for me, to be honest.
text_b: While entering the intersection at Rua das Flores, I miscalculated the timing of the traffic light change. A blue car coming from the cross street was already committed to the turn. We collided at a very low speed. My front left lamp is broken, and there's a dent on the fender. I am quite embarrassed because I usually pride myself on my driving record. I immediately checked on the other driver, and we exchanged details properly. I just want to make sure everything is handled correctly through the insurer.

text_a: A white sports car cut across three lanes at 120 km/h, causing a massive chain reaction behind me. The chaos forced me to swerve into the central divider. My front light is broken, the windshield is cracked, and I feel whiplash throughout my neck. The sports car didn't stop, and because of the multi-car pileup, nobody saw the plate. It's a complete nightmare scenario on the highway.
text_b: I was driving behind the Passat. There was absolutely nobody else on the road, no sports car, no pileup. He just drifted off the lane, hit the metal barrier on his own, and came to a stop. I was the only witness, and there was no other car involved.

text_a: I was reversing out of a parking spot near the downtown area, moving at maybe 5 km/h. I thought the path was clear, but I didn't notice the post right behind me. I heard a scraping sound and realized I had backed into it. There is a deep scratch on the rear bumper. I am quite embarrassed by this, it was a lapse in my concentration. I should have checked my sensors more carefully. I'm reporting this to get it repaired quickly as the car is fairly new.
text_b: I was sitting on the terrace of a nearby restaurant and saw the whole thing. The driver was backing up slowly and simply didn't see the bollard behind the car. It was just a minor accident, no one else was hurt, and the driver seemed very upset and apologetic about the damage caused to their own vehicle.

text_a: It was raining quite heavily this morning near the airport. I was navigating the roundabout, moving from the inside lane to exit, when another driver attempted to merge into my path too early. We collided at low speed as I was turning. I feel terrible about it, honestly, it's just so stressful. My front right indicator lamp is broken from the impact against their side door. I think I was following the rules, but I'm just really worried about how much this is going to cost to fix, man.
text_b: The road was very slippery due to the rain. I was exiting the roundabout and did not see the other car approaching in the outer lane. We made contact at the point of the indicator. My door has a scrape, and I noticed his lamp was broken during the incident.

text_a: I was proceeding cautiously over the Ponte 25 de Abril, maintaining a legal speed of precisely 70 km/h, well below the limit. I had not consumed any alcohol or impairing substances. Suddenly, a vehicle, which I believe was a black Mercedes, swiftly moved in front of me from the right lane, applied its brakes very sharply and unnecessarily. Despite my immediate and forceful braking action, I was unable to avoid a rear-end collision. My vehicle sustained significant damage to the front, including a dent, extensive scratches, and most notably, the windscreen shattered on impact. It was a completely unavoidable situation caused by the erratic driving of the other party, who then sped off.
text_b: I was driving a few cars behind. I saw a black Mercedes cut in front of an Audi very quickly and brake hard. The Audi didn't have time to react and hit it. The Mercedes then just drove away. The Audi had a lot of damage, especially the front windscreen, it looked like it shattered.

text_a: A dark-colored van forced me off the road while I was driving on a narrow municipal street in Gaia. To prevent a head-on collision, I steered into a stone wall, resulting in significant denting and deep scratches on the driver's side. The van sped away without stopping. It was a harrowing experience, and the speed at which the van crossed the center line was truly reckless. I am lucky to be alive, though my car is badly damaged and will require extensive structural repairs to be roadworthy again.
text_b: I was walking my dog on the sidewalk when the Volvo approached. The road was completely empty; no other vehicle was anywhere near the car. The driver simply steered into the wall at a low speed while looking at his phone.

text_a: At exactly 14:15, while I was traveling at a steady 30 km/h, the silver sedan entered the junction from the right and struck my front bumper with absolute precision. I was already braking, but there was zero chance to avoid the impact. It felt like the other driver planned this encounter perfectly, waiting for me to enter the clearing before lunging forward. I am completely sure they intended to hit my vehicle right at that specific angle to cause maximum disruption.
text_b: I was just driving along when this driver suddenly accelerated into my lane, giving me no room to react. Their vehicle just popped out of nowhere and drove directly into my side, which is why my car now has a significant dent.

text_a: The sunlight was blinding at the junction, and I failed to see the car coming from my right. It happened so fast; I felt a heavy impact on my passenger door and the side window shattered. I'm just thankful no one was sitting in that seat. My door is completely dented inward. I have never caused an accident like this and feel absolutely awful about it.
text_b: I had the right of way. He pulled out from the side street and I couldn't avoid him. My car impacted his side, causing my front end to crumple, but thankfully no one was injured. We both exited the vehicles to swap insurance info immediately.

text_a: I was heading towards the marina, and the traffic light turned yellow. I thought I could make it through, but the driver from the cross street started moving a bit early. We collided at the intersection. My front light is broken and the fender has a deep scratch. It was such a confusing moment, honestly, and I felt quite anxious about the whole scene. I just want to make sure the insurance process handles this correctly because I have never been in an accident before.
text_b: I was standing on the corner waiting to cross the street. The Citroën tried to beat the red light, but the other car entered the intersection just as it turned green. The impact was audible, and I saw the headlight lens break on the Citroën. Both drivers seemed genuinely shocked and stepped out of their vehicles immediately to inspect the damage.

text_a: Man, like, I was driving down Santa Catarina, just keeping in my lane, you know? And this delivery van just decided to switch lanes without looking and totally swiped the side of my car. I honked, but it was too late. There's a long scratch and a dent on my driver's door now. It's super annoying, pá.
text_b: I was waiting outside the Majestic Cafe. The Peugeot was going straight in the right lane. The white van in the left lane just drifted over without using a blinker and scraped the side of the Peugeot. The impact left a visible scratch and a small dent.

text_a: I was driving straight in the middle lane when a taxi suddenly swerved to avoid a cyclist. I had nowhere to go and ended up catching the back of the taxi with my side. There is a long scratch running along my driver's side door and a small dent near the handle. It all happened so fast, I didn't really have time to react. I'm just glad nobody got hit, especially the cyclist, though it was a very stressful moment for all of us involved in the traffic.
text_b: I was forced to shift quickly to avoid a cyclist who crossed into the lane without looking. I felt a scrape and heard a bang. The Nissan driver caught my rear bumper. There is a dent and several scratches on the side of my car. I stopped as soon as it was safe to do so to exchange details with the insured driver.

text_a: I was proceeding along Rua Augusta. Traffic ahead suddenly halted due to a pedestrian. I initiated braking maneuvers. The vehicle behind, a Renault Clio, failed to maintain an adequate safety distance and impacted my rear bumper. Impact speed estimated at 25 km/h. Minimal damage observed: minor dent to the rear bumper, superficial scratches. Driver appeared distressed but cooperative.
text_b: The driver of the Mercedes seemed to be moving specifically to ensure contact. He was driving quite slowly, almost waiting for me to pull up beside him before turning his wheel into my path.

text_a: I was inside a café when I heard a scraping sound outside. I went out to see this gentleman hitting my car while he was parking. There is a clear dent and a long scratch on the passenger side door. We have exchanged all the necessary insurance details now.
text_b: I was driving home from work around 6:30 PM, and the traffic on Avenida da Boavista was incredibly heavy as usual. I was slowing down because the car in front of me stopped suddenly, and I managed to brake in time, but the driver behind me didn't. He hit my rear bumper quite hard. I am really worried because this is my only car for commuting, and I have never dealt with an accident claim before. It just feels like a big dent right in the middle of the bumper, and I really hope the repair process is straightforward.

text_a: I was maneuvering into a parking spot. A man suddenly jumped behind my vehicle just as I started reversing. I stopped, but there was already a dent. He was acting very strangely, looking at his watch repeatedly and insisting I pay him in cash immediately instead of calling the police.
text_b: I saw the pedestrian walk up to the car while it was already stopped. He actually walked into the bumper on purpose and then acted like he was hit. The driver seemed genuinely confused and frightened by the man's demands.

text_a: I was driving in the lane next to the Peugeot. They lost control on the oil patch and hit the divider themselves. There was no other car involved, certainly no SUV in sight at the time of the impact.
text_b: The traffic in front of me stopped suddenly near the roundabout entrance. I braked as hard as I could, but my tires skidded on the oily surface of the road. I hit the back of the car ahead, resulting in my front lamp breaking and a dent in the bumper. I've already spoken to the other driver and we have exchanged all our details. I'm feeling quite bad about it, but I'm glad nobody got injured in the process.

text_a: I was driving responsibly on the IC19, maintaining a speed of approximately 90 km/h, well within the limit. Suddenly, a dark-colored vehicle, I believe a Mercedes E-Class, aggressively swerved in front of me from the right lane without warning and immediately braked hard. I had absolutely no time to react. I applied maximum brake pressure, but a collision was unavoidable. My front bumper sustained a significant dent, extensive scratches, my headlight is broken, and the windshield has a massive crack. This was clearly the other driver's fault; I was not intoxicated or distracted in any way.
text_b: I was just driving, and the car behind me, a Seat Ibiza, was following too closely. I had to brake because of traffic ahead, and they hit me. There's only a minor scratch on my bumper, but they're claiming all sorts of damage. I don't know why they're so upset.

text_a: I was driving across the 25 de Abril Bridge heading toward Almada around 8:00 AM. Traffic was moving at about 40 km/h when I checked my mirror to move into the left lane. I failed to see the motorcycle coming up in my blind spot. We made contact, which caused a scratch and a small dent on my passenger door. I am incredibly worried because I didn't see him at all. I have been driving for years and this has never happened to me.
text_b: I was driving in the lane next to them when the incident occurred. It was clearly an honest mistake as the weather conditions were a bit misty and the visibility was reduced. The driver of the Ford attempted a lane change and simply did not see the other vehicle coming up behind them. Both parties stopped safely immediately after.

text_a: I was driving through the intersection when suddenly a delivery driver sprinted into the side of my car. It was such a strange occurrence, like the vehicle came out of nowhere to catch the side door. The window shattered instantly and there is a massive dent. I am convinced this was a setup to collect insurance money from me, given how they appeared to speed up right at the point of impact.
text_b: The Audi driver didn't check their surroundings. I was proceeding normally through the intersection and they swerved into my path, causing the collision. I was not speeding at all.

text_a: I was proceeding through the green light at the intersection when the other driver ignored the red signal and T-boned my vehicle with full force. My passenger side lamp is broken, but the force of the collision was such that it pushed my entire engine block sideways. I insist on a full claim for the internal structural chassis collapse.
text_b: I was absolutely within my rights, passing through the junction under green lights. The BMW accelerated specifically to hit my side. It looked planned from the start, almost as if he was waiting for me to get close before maneuvering to ensure the impact occurred exactly where it did.

text_a: I was stopped in the line of traffic. The car behind me didn't stop in time and nudged my rear. It is just a minor scratch on my bumper. No major problems to report, and we handled the paperwork right there.
text_b: I was driving along the Estrada Monumental, moving slowly due to the heavy tourist traffic. I was looking for a parking spot for a restaurant. I got distracted for a split second by a sign and didn't notice the car in front of me had come to a complete stop. I hit the rear of the car at probably 10 km/h. There is a small dent on my hood and a corresponding dent on their bumper. I feel really foolish for being so distracted while driving.

text_a: I was walking by the shop when I saw the Toyota attempting to parallel park. The driver seemed to be struggling with the space and unfortunately, they misjudged the turning radius. They lightly scraped the side of the parked vehicle. Both the Toyota and the other car ended up with some visible cosmetic damage, specifically a dent and a scratch.
text_b: I was walking my dog on the sidewalk when I heard the impact. I looked over and saw only the Nissan parked by the curb. There was absolutely no other car present at the scene of the collision, only the insured driver staring at his bumper.

text_a: Everything was perfectly aligned when he suddenly sped through the red light at exactly 15:45. My vehicle was stationary, yet he hit me with such force that my chassis should have folded like paper. I am incredibly shaken, but I have already contacted my lawyer. Please ensure the settlement reflects the massive structural stress my vehicle endured, even if the exterior crack looks small.
text_b: The other driver is lying completely. I was rolling slowly at about 5 km/h behind him when he suddenly slammed his brakes on a clear road. I barely tapped his rear bumper. He jumped out screaming before I even touched his car.

text_a: Oh God, I'm so shaken, pá. I was approaching the traffic lights, you know, the ones near the Mercado do Livramento. It turned green, I swear! And then this other car, a small grey one, just came straight through the red. I swerved but couldn't avoid it. There's like, a big dent on my front right fender, and my headlamp is definitely broken. I really hope my insurance covers this, I can't afford a huge bill.
text_b: I was waiting at the bus stop, just watching people, when the light for the Dacia definitely went red. The Dacia accelerated instead of stopping. The Seat then hit it. The Seat has a smashed light and a dent. The Dacia only a small mark. It was very clear the Dacia ran the red light.

text_a: Narrow streets in Coimbra are always a nightmare. I was slowly reversing out of a parking spot near the university area when I misjudged the proximity of the bollard. However, as I corrected, another car came around the corner too fast and hit the corner of my bumper. It wasn't a huge hit, but there is definitely a noticeable dent there now. I feel so embarrassed about it. I have never had an incident like this before and I'm honestly quite worried about what this will do to my insurance premium next year.
text_b: I was parking my Skoda on the street, which is quite narrow, and I must have misjudged the proximity to the car behind me. As I shifted to reverse, I bumped gently into the front bumper of the parked vehicle. There is a small dent and a long, noticeable scratch on my rear bumper. I feel terrible about it. I have been driving for many years and rarely have these kinds of mishaps. I have already left my contact details on the windshield of the other car, and I am ready to handle the insurance process appropriately.

text_a: I was just trying to reverse into a spot, going like, 5 km/h, really slow. This big SUV, a Mercedes GLC, just swiped my passenger side. It was barely a touch, but it left a really deep scratch, and somehow the impact also caused a dent in the door panel AND my rear tail lamp is completely broken. It must have been a weird angle, I suppose. It's a bit blurry, but that's what I saw when I checked.
text_b: I saw the Mercedes swerving. There was absolutely no other car in front of him. He hit the brakes and the glass seemed to break from something inside or a stone kicked up by his own wheels.

text_a: Oh dear, it was such a lovely day, I was going to the Forum to buy some fabric for my granddaughter's dress, you see, she just turned seven. And as I was backing out of my parking spot, very slowly, mind you, only like 5 km/h, I just, well, I didn't see that little post on my left. My lovely Corsa, it got a dent and some horrible scratches on the back bumper. My husband, Manuel, he's going to be so upset, he loves this car. I'm not good with all this technology, but I think I filled out the form correctly, bless you.
text_b: I was walking past, heading to the cinema, when I saw an older lady in an Opel Corsa slowly reversing out of a parking spot. She seemed to misjudge the distance and bumped directly into a concrete pillar. There was a clear scraping sound, and I saw a dent forming on her rear bumper, along with some paint scratches. She looked quite distressed.

text_a: I was driving to the supermarket on a beautiful morning, thinking about my grandchildren visiting later this week, when I reached the intersection near the hotel. The traffic light was green, but a driver coming from the side street didn't seem to notice his stop sign. He drove right out and struck the side of my car. My driver-side window glass shattered everywhere and there is a significant dent in the door. It was quite a shock, really. I am just thankful that I wasn't going any faster when he hit me, honestly.
text_b: I was standing on the corner waiting for the bus when I saw the whole thing happen. The Toyota was clearly moving within the speed limit, and the other vehicle failed to stop at the stop sign entirely. It resulted in a loud crash. I saw the glass shatter and the door buckle inward. I am happy to provide my contact details as I saw that the Toyota driver was clearly not at fault.

text_a: I didn't stop fast enough and nudged the car ahead. It was just a small dent, but I’m worried about the other person. They were quite insistent on calling an ambulance, claiming severe whiplash despite the low impact speed. I really hope my policy covers their medical expenses, as they are asking for a significant settlement for their back pain.
text_b: I was stationary when I was hit with significant force. The collision was violent enough that I've been feeling extreme neck stiffness since the incident. I am currently seeking medical evaluation for this injury.

text_a: Someone tapped my car in the parking lot and smashed my tail light. Not only is the lamp broken, but the vibration shattered my rear window completely. It is going to be incredibly expensive to replace the glass and the lighting assembly. I don't know who did it, but the damage is extensive. The whole rear end looks like a disaster zone. I hope the coverage accounts for the interior glass shards as well, as they are everywhere.
text_b: I saw a delivery driver reverse slowly and hit the bumper of the Polo. The tail lamp broke, but the window remained completely intact. The driver is exaggerating about the glass being shattered.

text_a: It was raining quite heavily near the roundabout. Traffic suddenly halted, and I tapped the brakes, but the road surface was slicker than I anticipated. My Polo slid a few meters, making contact with the car in front at a low speed. I am honestly quite shaken up as this is my first time dealing with a collision. My front bumper seems to have a deep dent and some paint damage, which matches the assessment.
text_b: The driver behind me just misjudged the stopping distance in the wet weather. My car was completely stationary at the red light when I felt the impact. I stepped out to find my rear bumper scratched and dented, but thankfully everyone is okay.

text_a: It was during the morning rush hour on the bridge. A dark gray sports car aggressively cut between lanes, clipped my front bumper, and then vanished into the thick bridge traffic. I barely kept control of the steering wheel. There are long, deep scratches all along the side of my car and a cracked mirror. It's frustrating that such reckless people exist on the road, creating danger for everyone else. I am just lucky I didn't hit the barrier.
text_b: I saw the Megane swerve on its own while trying to adjust lanes. There were no other vehicles within ten meters of that car when the incident occurred.

text_a: A silver van swerved violently into my lane while crossing the bridge. I had to brake hard to avoid it, which caused the car behind me to smash into my rear. The phantom van just drove away without stopping. My rear windshield has a large crack from the sudden pressure, and I believe the stress fracture to the rear axle is also a direct result of this reckless driver.
text_b: There was absolutely no other car present. The Tesla driver just slammed on the brakes for no reason while traffic was flowing perfectly fine at 80 km/h. I had zero time to react to such erratic behavior on the bridge.

text_a: I was driving down Avenida da Boavista during the morning rush hour. Traffic was quite heavy, and the vehicle in front of me suddenly braked hard because of a pedestrian crossing. I tried to press my brake pedal, but I was just too close and ended up bumping into his rear bumper at a very low speed. I feel terrible about it, honestly. My front bumper has a noticeable dent and some deep scratches from the impact. I am so worried about the repair costs, you know, it has just been such a stressful morning.
text_b: I was moving slowly in the middle lane when I had to stop abruptly for a person crossing the street. I felt a sudden jolt from behind. The other driver apologized immediately and was very cooperative. We pulled over to the side to exchange information. My rear bumper clearly shows a dent and some paint scratches where his car hit me.

text_a: Oh my god, like, I was just driving really slowly, you know? On Rua João Mendonça, near the canals, and this guy, he just stepped out into the road without looking, pá. I braked really hard, but I, like, just barely touched him. He fell, but he seemed okay, just a bit shaken. My car has a small dent on the front bumper. Is he okay? Will I get a fine, dude? I'm so worried.
text_b: Yes, I saw it, poor boy, it was quite sad. I was just heading to the bakery, like I do every morning, for my morning bread. The driver, a young girl, was going very slow, maybe 10 km/h, and the gentleman, he was looking at his phone, you know how these young people are. He just walked right out. The car barely nudged him, he just stumbled and fell. A small dent on the car, yes, I saw that. He seemed fine, just a bit of a shock, like when you drop your keys.

text_a: I tapped his bumper with my rubber step. I checked it, and it was a simple scratch. He is complaining about internal mechanical systems which have absolutely nothing to do with a gentle side contact.
text_b: I was cruising along the EN125 near Faro when a dark sedan swerved into my lane without signaling. To avoid a head-on collision, I jerked the steering wheel hard to the right and hit a concrete bollard. The mysterious driver never stopped; they just sped off into the sunset. My windshield is cracked from the impact debris, and I expect the insurance to handle the massive costs of the structural frame repair which clearly happened during this high-stakes maneuver.

text_b: I was stopped completely behind a stationary line of traffic due to the signal change. Suddenly, I felt a heavy impact from behind. My car was pushed forward, resulting in a noticeable dent and several scratches on the rear trunk lid. It was clearly the fault of the person behind me.

I have the police report number from the officers who arrived shortly after the incident occurred.
text_b: The traffic signal turned amber while I was in the middle of the intersection. I tried to accelerate to clear it, but I caught the passenger side of the Nissan. I failed to stop in time to avoid the contact.

I demand full compensation for the severe mechanical failure and the total body destruction caused by this irresponsible party.
text_b: It was just a low-speed tap in traffic. There was only a minor dent on the bumper. The other driver is clearly inflating the extent of the impact to get more money.
